edges.description: Absent or nonfunctional glycogenin-1 cannot prime glycogen synthesis normally.

edges.description: In the founding case, inactivated priming instead depleted glycogen in skeletal muscle.

Polyglucosan and glycogen deposits disrupt muscle fibers, causing progressive weakness.

nodes.description: Glycogenin-1 normally autoglucosylates to build the short oligosaccharide primer that glycogen synthase and branching enzyme extend into glycogen. Loss of this priming activity disrupts normal glycogen synthesis in muscle.

evidence.reference_title: Glycogenin-1 deficiency and inactivated priming of glycogen synthesis.
evidence.snippet: The missense mutation resulted in inactivation of the autoglucosylation of glycogenin-1 that is necessary for the priming of glycogen synthesis in muscle.
